Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/DPA redlines for connector partnership

Karthik —

Thanks for the productive call last week. Our legal team reviewed the template MSA, DPA and the draft SOW you sent and attached a consolidated set of redlines (MSA_RL_v3). Key asks from our side:

- Data residency language: require that customer data originating from US customers remain within US regions unless explicitly requested.
- Audit rights: 60 days' advance notice for on-site audits; remote evidence acceptable for security reports.
- Indemnity cap: prefer a 1x ARR cap; open to negotiation tied to confirmed usage tiers.
- Subprocessors: require a 30-day notice and approval right for any new subprocessors that handle customer PII.

I've attached the redline and an edited DPA for reference. Procurement looped in on cc to help with timeline. Can we get Redwood's position on the residency clause and subprocessors by EOD Wednesday?

Regards,
Jenny Park
Head of Partnerships — StratAlliance
Jenny Park | StratAlliance, Inc.

Jenny — thanks for sending these and for the clear call notes. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Ben (partnerships/dev) so we can triage. Quick ack and proposed next steps: 

1) Residency: Redwood's hosted API supports region pinning; we can commit to US-only processing for StratAlliance-managed customers if the account-level config is captured in the SOW and the volume & retention are within the expected tiers. Need: a short clause in SOW plus a small ops playbook.

2) Subprocessors: we can accept notice + right to object for new subprocessors that process PII. For operational scale we typically provide a 30-day notice and a mitigation plan; for critical subprocessors we'll offer a short escalation SLA.

3) Indemnity: our standard is a capped liability at 1x ARR for commercial claims; for IP-specific claims we keep standard carveouts. We should align on whether ARR is measured at contract signature or trailing 12M — propose trailing 12M.

Marissa — can you review the redlines and call out any absolute no-go items? If possible, I'd like to propose a one-page security annex that references SOC 2 + the annex controls rather than expanding the MSA. That keeps the MSA cleaner for procurement.

Proposed timeline: legal comments by Tue EOD (you), counter redline Wed AM (us), DocuSign by next Tue. Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications from StratAlliance legal:

- Residency: the ask is not only for processing but for storage of customer outputs (embeddings, logs). We need a contractual guarantee  that backups or cached artifacts storing US-customer outputs remain in US regions unless customer opts in.
- Audit: 60 days is preferred; we will accept remote SOC2 + on-demand evidence for 3rd party scans. On-site audits will be limited and subject to timeline constraints.
- Data deletion: require formal deletion SLA for cached prefixes/KV within 30 days of contract termination for customers who request deletion.

I've attached an edited DPA that reflects those points. We're flexible on indemnity cap but will need a short mutuality clause for data breach scenarios.

Michael Zhou
Senior Counsel — StratAlliance
Phone: +1 (212) 555-0123

Attachment: StratAlliance_DPA_v2.pdf (pdf, 46KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Zhou <michael.zhou@stratalliance.com>, Jenny Park <jenny@stratalliance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA/DPA redlines for connector partnership

Michael / Jenny — appreciate the detail. We reviewed with engineering and legal — responses inline below and a proposed compromise: 

- Storage/residency: We can commit to US-region storage for customer-originated outputs and caches when the account is flagged as US-only in the SOW. Operational note: this requires a small ops runbook to confirm no cross-region backups for those accounts. We'll include that as an annex (Security Annex, see attached draft).

- Data deletion: Redwood can offer a 30-day deletion SLA for cached KV/prefixes on contract termination for customers who opt into deletion in the SOW. For backups retained by third-party cloud providers, we will document retention windows and provide deletion certificates where possible.

- Audit & SOC2: We'll provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report and a periodic third-party scan summary. On-site audits will be governed by the notice period and a scoped checklist.

- Indemnity mutuality: propose the indemnity be mutual for IP claims; for data breaches, propose a shared-cap approach with a per-claim cap tied to 1x ARR and an aggregator cap at 2x ARR. If this is a hard blocker, please flag and we'll escalate.

Attached is a one-page proposed mutual action plan to get us to signature: 
- Thu 20 May: exchange redlines (legal)
- Fri 21 May: exec sign-off window
- Tue 25 May: DocuSign envelope live

Can you confirm whether procurement needs a PO first or if DocuSign is sufficient to start onboarding? Also sending the draft Security Annex now.

Thanks,
Karthik
---

Michael / Jenny —

Appreciate the clarity here. Redwood legal has reviewed the StratAlliance edits and we can accept the majority of the DPA redlines with the following clarifications to be captured in the redline: 

1) Definition of "customer data" — we will adopt StratAlliance's proposed language but explicitly exclude aggregated telemetry that cannot be reverse-engineered to a specific customer.
2) Subprocessors — we will provide a rolling list of subprocessors and 30 days' notice; note that for cloud infra (major cloud providers) we treat those as non-consent subprocessors but will provide SOC2 evidence.
3) Data deletion — we will commit to 30 day deletion of hot caches and provide a deletion certificate for manifestable deletes; archival backups will follow cloud provider retention and we will notify customers of the same.
4) Indemnity — we accept mutual IP indemnity; for breach-related liability, Redwood requests caps as discussed by Karthik (1x ARR per event, 2x ARR aggregate).

Attached is Redwood's redline to the MSA (MSA_Redline_from_Redwood_v1) — please confirm the SOW/ops playbook attachment so we can finalize residency obligations. Once you confirm, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope (link below) and sync on the HubSpot deal (link below).
